Subject: Intermittent partial payloads observed — status & next steps

Hi Alex,

We detected intermittent partial responses (truncated JSON bodies / early stream termination) affecting Folio Health traffic to our hosted generation API between 08:40–09:05 PST this morning. We immediately opened an incident (INF-2267) and published a status page entry: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INF-2267

What we know so far:
- Affected endpoint: POST /v1/generate (streaming responses)
- Symptom: clients received syntactically incomplete response bodies (JSON ending mid-object) or an early EOF during streaming
- Window: ~08:40–09:05 PST; impact most visible under high fanout (many concurrent small requests)
- Initial mitigation: temporarily pinned traffic to warmed instances and flushed prefix KV cache for the affected partition

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether any of your production clients retried aggressively or logged parser errors? If you can share a short sample of client-facing failures that would help our triage.

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (timeline + hits per region)

We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a technical summary and remediation plan. We'll propose a make-good if your usage was materially impacted.

Sorry for the disruption — will update in ~30 mins or when we have more.

— Priyom
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Folks,

Forwarding the Folio thread. TL;DR of our triage so far:
- Root cause (current hypothesis): cascading KV-prefix evictions during a burst led to frequent cache-misses mid-stream; combined with our streaming termination logic, a race caused the stream to close without finalizing the response envelope.
- Why it affected Folio disproportionately: their usage pattern has high-concurrency short requests (fanout) which amplified the race.
- Immediate mitigations applied: pinned traffic to warmed pools, increased streaming window timeout from 1s -> 3s for affected instances, single-partition KV flush to avoid repeated eviction churn.
- Long-term fixes planned: safer stream-finalization path (backfill on stream loss), conservative eviction backoff, and a short release (runtime 0.8.7) to harden the path.

I drafted a postmortem and uploaded it (postmortem-draft.docx). I also suggested offering Folio a 5% invoice credit for the impacted hour and expedited SLA review. Ben — can you confirm the suggested credit and engage finance if needed? Marissa — can you coordinate a 30-min customer call (we should offer 11:30 PST today)? Laura — please add a short note to the status page that we have a postmortem draft available and will publish within 72 hours.

— Priyom

Hi Alex — thanks again for the sample logs.

We've completed our initial post-incident analysis and published a concise summary on the incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INF-2267

Executive summary:
- What happened: under high-concurrency fanout, a cascade of prefix-KV evictions created a race during streaming response finalization. The runtime occasionally closed the connection before emitting the final framing token, which produced truncated JSON in-flight.
- Impact window: 08:40–09:05 PST on 2026-11-30
- Customers affected: subset of streaming clients, more visible for high-fanout patterns (your logs matched this pattern)
- Immediate remediation: traffic pinned to warmed instances, increased stream finalization timeout, targeted KV partition flush
- Permanent fixes: 0.8.7 runtime patch to ensure atomic stream finalization, eviction backoff introduced in the cache layer, and an observability alert for incomplete response-body counts

Make-good: we're proposing a 5% credit for usage during the 08:40–09:05 PST window. If you'd like, we can escalate to a 10% credit pending any material billing delta you find — please share the billing window and sample counters.

Next steps:
- We will publish a full postmortem within 72 hours and share a follow-up meeting invite (requested 11:30 PST today — we'll confirm)
- Links & artifacts: incident_timeline.csv (attached), postmortem draft (private link on request), incident page https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INF-2267

If you prefer a walk-through of the technical fixes, Ben/Marissa and I are available to join a call.

Apologies for the disruption — we take this seriously.

— Priyom Das
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
